mechanism_log: The system is driven by a small number of key inputs with clear causal roles. Y3 is almost entirely determined by X1+X3 (linear, R²=0.91). Y2 is mainly driven by X3 (negative) and X4 (negative). Y1 is driven by X4 (monotonic, strong), X5 (positive but saturates at ~0.5), X1, and X3. Y4 is driven by X4 and X2. Critically: X11 shows ZERO causal effect in two separate OAT tests despite a global correlation of -0.60 with Y1 — this correlation is spurious/confounding. Similarly X7-X12 all have zero local gradients. Most objectives are aligned (high X4 helps Y1, Y2, Y4 simultaneously; high X1 and X3 helps Y3 and Y2). The main trade-off is between Y3 (needs high X1+X3) and potentially Y1/Y4 optimization levers.

The system is driven by a small number of causal inputs with clear, confirmed roles. Y3 is almost entirely determined by X1+X3 (linear, R²=0.91). Y1 and Y4 are dominated by an X2×X4 product interaction — local gradient dY1/dX2=0.807 at X4=1.0 vs regression coef 0.332 at mean X4, perfectly explained by a multiplicative term. Y2 is driven by X2 (positive) and X1/X3/X4 (negative), with a regime-dependent X6×X2 interaction: X6 increases Y2 at mid-range X1/X2/X3, but DECREASES Y2 at all-max values. The main Pareto trade-off has two dimensions: (1) X2 level controls Y1↑/Y4↑/Y2↑ simultaneously; (2) X6 level at the all-max regime controls Y1↑/Y2↓/Y4↓. X5 saturates completely above ~0.5 and has zero effect on any output above that threshold. X7-X12 (except X6) are causally inactive — their correlations with outputs are spurious. Best achievable Y1=1.131 (at X1=X2=X3=X4=1.0, X6=1.0), best Y2=0.071 (at X1=X3=X4=1.0, X2=0.1, X6=0.1), best Y4=0.322 (at X1=X2=X3=X4=1.0, X6=0.1).

iteration_summaries.hypothesis: The system is driven by a small number of causal inputs with clear, confirmed roles. Y3 is almost entirely determined by X1+X3 (linear, R²=0.91). Y1 and Y4 are dominated by an X2×X4 product interaction — local gradient dY1/dX2=0.807 at X4=1.0 vs regression coef 0.332 at mean X4, perfectly explained by a multiplicative term. Y2 is driven by X2 (positive) and X1/X3/X4 (negative), with a regime-dependent X6×X2 interaction: X6 increases Y2 at mid-range X1/X2/X3, but DECREASES Y2 at all-max values. The main Pareto trade-off has two dimensions: (1) X2 level controls Y1↑/Y4↑/Y2↑ simultaneously; (2) X6 level at the all-max regime controls Y1↑/Y2↓/Y4↓. X5 saturates completely above ~0.5 and has zero effect on any output above that threshold. X7-X12 (except X6) are causally inactive — their correlations with outputs are spurious. Best achievable Y1=1.131 (at X1=X2=X3=X4=1.0, X6=1.0), best Y2=0.071 (at X1=X3=X4=1.0, X2=0.1, X6=0.1), best Y4=0.322 (at X1=X2=X3=X4=1.0, X6=0.1).
new_findings: Y1 can reach 1.131 — more than 2.6× the previous observed best of 0.433. Previous experiments severely undersampled the favorable X2/X6 regime.
Y2 can reach 0.071 — 63% below the previous best of 0.193, achieved at X2=0.1 with X1=X3=X4=1.0.
X2×X4 product interaction confirmed: at X4=1.0, dY1/dX2=0.807; at mean X4≈0.55, effective coef=0.332. The interaction coefficient ≈1.056 with direct X2 term ≈-0.249.

X6 has a REGIME-DEPENDENT effect on Y2: at all-max (X1=X2=X3=X4=1.0), increasing X6 from 0.1→1.0 DECREASES Y2 from 0.362→0.303 while increasing Y1 from 0.948→1.131. At the previous midpoint base, X6→Y2 was positive (+0.086). Sign reversal = X6×X2 interaction.
X5 is completely inert above 0.5: X5=0.7 and X5=1.0 yield IDENTICAL outputs to 4 decimal places at Y1=0.9478, Y2=0.3617, Y3=0.9973, Y4=0.3218.
Y3 is essentially binary at all-max conditions: X1=X3=1.0 gives Y3=0.9973 regardless of other inputs. Only fails when X1+X3 is insufficient (X1=X3=0.35 gives Y3=0.388, below threshold).

The X6 sweep at X2=1.0 traces a clean Pareto curve: X6=0.1→Y4=0.322 (best Y4), X6=1.0→Y1=1.131,Y2=0.303 (best Y1 and competitive Y2). Each step increases X6 by 0.2 increases Y1 by ~0.05-0.09, decreases Y2 by ~0.01-0.02, decreases Y4 by ~0.017.
surprises: Y1=1.131 exceeded expectations dramatically — predicted 0.6 for the all-max point. The X2×X4 synergy is non-additive and causes Y1 to far exceed simple linear sum predictions.
X6→Y2 reversed sign in the high-X1/X2/X3 regime. The same input that hurt Y2 at midpoints now HELPS it. This was completely unpredicted and revealed a strong X6×X2 interaction term.

X5=1.0 and X5=0.7 give LITERALLY identical outputs (4-decimal match). The saturation is a hard plateau, not a gradual diminishing return. X5 effectively becomes a binary variable: active above ~0.4, irrelevant above ~0.5.

At X6=1.0 with X2=0.2, Y4=0.049 is surprisingly low — X6 penalty on Y4 plus low X2×X4 product combine to crush Y4 despite X4=1.0. Y4 is nearly entirely explained by X2×X4 product with minimal direct X4 term.
Previous best Pareto front had hypervolume 0.0935 with only 5 non-dominated points; now the front is dramatically expanded with Y1 ranging 0.049–1.131 and Y2 ranging 0.071–0.362.
iteration_summaries.next_plan: Budget exhausted. If more evals were available: (1) Map the 2D (X2, X6) trade-off surface with a grid of 3×3 experiments to find Pareto-optimal diagonal; (2) Test whether X6=0.7 with X2=0.85 gives Y1>1.0 with Y4>0.27 and Y2<0.30 simultaneously; (3) Verify whether any other inputs (X2×X1 or X2×X3 interactions) contribute to Y4; (4) Check if Y3 threshold can be met with X1=X3=0.3 by adjusting other inputs.
